programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
International Men’s Day was established in 1999 to highlight positive male role models and raise awareness of men’s health and wellbeing. Ahead of this year’s event, Sean Fletcher is in Leeds exploring what it means to be a man in modern society, and how faith, friendship and a sense of purpose can help men thrive in mind, body and spirit.
He meets rugby league legend Jamie Jones-Buchanan, now CEO of Leeds Rhinos, where he made 421 appearances, as well as representing England and Great Britain. Jamie reflects on growing up without a father figure in one of the UK’s most deprived areas, and how rugby and his Christian faith provided positive male role models, and a sense of belonging and purpose. He challenges stereotypes of the macho rugby player, and his passion for helping the next generation comes to life during a training session.
In the Welsh valleys, Pastor John Funnell reflects on the extraordinary number of young men joining his congregation. John left a highly paid career after becoming a Christian and moved to one of Europe’s most deprived communities. He explains how his church offers practical skills, mentoring, friendship and faith, helping men see that their past does not have to determine their future.
Back in Leeds, Sean meets Chris Sayburn, a minister and renowned worship leader who spent 12 years living with chronic pain following complications after spinal surgery. He tells Sean how exercise and faith have helped him rebuild his life and how a community of men became a lifeline.
With uplifting hymns and songs from around the UK.
1. Sweet Heart of Jesus - Leeds Cathedral 2. Amazing Grace - The Kingdom Choir 3. Facing a Task Unfinished - Lisburn Cathedral 4. Lord of All Hopefulness - Chris Sayburn and Friends 5. programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The open ocean is the largest wilderness on earth. Covering more than half of the planet's surface, it appears at first glance to be an endless blue desert. Yet hidden here are some of the most extraordinary animals.
We uncover the surprising strategies, epic journeys and remarkable resilience that allows life to thrive here. From wandering predators and drifting castaways to giant whales and tiny turtle hatchlings, it is a world where life survives against the odds.
The journey begins far beyond the sight of land, where California sea lions travel miles into the Pacific in search of seasonal, rich fishing grounds. Here, they join one of the open ocean's great feeding spectacles as black skipjack tuna, mahi-mahi and seabirds converge on vast schools of fish in a dramatic battle for a meal.
Some animals aren’t just visitors here; they spend their entire lives in this immense expanse. Rough-toothed dolphins have roamed the oceans since before woolly mammoths walked the earth, and yet we know very little about them. To help find food, they use sophisticated teamwork and ingenious hunting techniques that have rarely been witnessed.
Although the open ocean seems like a featureless expanse, it is shaped by powerful currents that flow across the globe like invisible rivers. These currents transport animals, nutrients and entire ecosystems across immense distances. For ocean drifters such as Smith's swimming crabs, the currents are both a lifeline and a gamble, carrying them through a world where danger can appear without warning.
Currents also drive one of the largest floating ecosystems on the planet. Today, the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt stretches over 5,000 miles across the ocean. But changing conditions are sweeping unprecedented amounts of this seaweed onto coastlines throughout the Caribbean. On the beaches of Mexico, turtle hatchlings emerging from their nests face a daunting new obstacle as mountains of sargassum block their path to the sea. Their struggle reveals how changes in the open ocean can have profound consequences far beyond the horizon.
In the Pacific, we follow one of nature's greatest aerial pirates, a frigatebird mother raising her chick alone.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here.
Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey - black-necked swans.
Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace - a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves.
As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable - they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before.
As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The open ocean is the largest wilderness on earth. Covering more than half of the planet's surface, it appears at first glance to be an endless blue desert. Yet hidden here are some of the most extraordinary animals.
We uncover the surprising strategies, epic journeys and remarkable resilience that allows life to thrive here. From wandering predators and drifting castaways to giant whales and tiny turtle hatchlings, it is a world where life survives against the odds.
The journey begins far beyond the sight of land, where California sea lions travel miles into the Pacific in search of seasonal, rich fishing grounds. Here, they join one of the open ocean's great feeding spectacles as black skipjack tuna, mahi-mahi and seabirds converge on vast schools of fish in a dramatic battle for a meal.
Some animals aren’t just visitors here; they spend their entire lives in this immense expanse. Rough-toothed dolphins have roamed the oceans since before woolly mammoths walked the earth, and yet we know very little about them. To help find food, they use sophisticated teamwork and ingenious hunting techniques that have rarely been witnessed.
Although the open ocean seems like a featureless expanse, it is shaped by powerful currents that flow across the globe like invisible rivers. These currents transport animals, nutrients and entire ecosystems across immense distances. For ocean drifters such as Smith's swimming crabs, the currents are both a lifeline and a gamble, carrying them through a world where danger can appear without warning.
Currents also drive one of the largest floating ecosystems on the planet. Today, the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt stretches over 5,000 miles across the ocean. But changing conditions are sweeping unprecedented amounts of this seaweed onto coastlines throughout the Caribbean. On the beaches of Mexico, turtle hatchlings emerging from their nests face a daunting new obstacle as mountains of sargassum block their path to the sea. Their struggle reveals how changes in the open ocean can have profound consequences far beyond the horizon.
In the Pacific, we follow one of nature's greatest aerial pirates, a frigatebird mother raising her chick alone.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc:
In the late 1980s, the British culinary scene was dominated by the traditions and techniques of French cuisine, and the kitchen hierarchy was rigid and unforgiving. Then, a working-class northerner with no interest in the rules became the most talked-about chef in the country. Marco Pierre White burst onto the scene and changed the future of British gastronomy, setting the standard that Gordon Ramsay and Heston Blumenthal would later be measured against.
The story begins with the opening of Harvey’s in 1987, the restaurant that made Marco's name. Contributors, including Marcus Wareing, Michel Roux Jr, Angela Hartnett, Clare Smyth and Tom Kerridge, reflect on what it meant to cook in the shadow of France and how Marco mastered the classical foundations before tearing up the rule book.
Into this world came a young Gordon Ramsay, hungry to learn and determined to prove himself. Under Marco's wing, he was tested to the limit. Gordon's remarkable stamina and his ability to learn quickly are explored, along with the stories that became kitchen legend, including falling asleep on the job during 18-hour shifts. Former colleagues and fellow chefs recall a driven newcomer who absorbed everything around him, and the bond, part mentorship and part rivalry, that took shape between teacher and pupil.
Meanwhile, a third force was emerging from a very different direction. Heston Blumenthal worked alongside Marco but shunned the traditional route to excellence, approaching cooking as a scientist might, asking why food behaves as it does and turning those answers into a fresh vision of what fine dining could achieve. His experimental mindset lifted the gastronomic experience to heights nobody had imagined and added a new dimension to the revolution already reshaping British cooking.
Set against the backdrop of the 'Cool Britannia' era of radical social and cultural change, the series explores a decade when fashion, politics and music were being torn up and rewritten. Another rock 'n' roll revolution was happening in the UK, this time in the kitchen. The story is one of rivalry and the pursuit of perfection, where the real heat was not just in the kitchen.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.sub-title: The Devil Is in Him ║ S1E3/6
programme.desc: After a hair-raising drive across the Conor Pass and a spot of seaside silliness hitting golf balls into the ocean, Bill bids farewell to Chris O'Dowd. In County Clare, Bill and Tom's attempt to sneak unnoticed into a hurling match goes awry, before an emotional reunion recalls an unforgettable act of kindness. Then, a chance invitation in Ballybunion leads to a freezing Atlantic challenge.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
Six ambitious chefs enter the MasterChef kitchen ready to prove they have what it takes to succeed in the competition. Across two demanding challenges, they’ll need to demonstrate skill, creativity and precision to impress renowned chef Monica Galetti and culinary legend Marcus Wareing. Only those who can deliver excellence under pressure will make it through.
First up, the famous skills test returns, but there is a twist. In the studio, the chefs discover that they won’t face it alone. Instead, they must compete side by side, intensifying the pressure. The aim is to recreate a technical dish designed by the judges. There’s little room for error, with every decision laid bare. Every chop, slice and saute will be under scrutiny not just from Monica and Marcus but each other.
Monica has set the bar high with a technical crab raviolo dish, served with a rich, deeply flavoured bisque. First, the chefs must tackle the crab, which involves cracking the shell without any shards making it into the dish. Then comes the bisque, where they’ll need to coax maximum flavour from the crab to create a sauce worthy of the finished plate. For one chef, the bisque is a technique they’ve never attempted before, while another struggles with the consistency of their pasta and finds it increasingly difficult to keep their cool. As tensions and emotions run high, can the chefs pull everything together and deliver a restaurant-quality plate, or will the intense pressure of the skills test prove too much?
The heat ends with all six chefs returning to the kitchen for one final chance to impress the judges with their signature dish. They must showcase the food that defines them, pushing their culinary creativity to the limit in the hope of securing a place in the next round. But with the standard higher than ever, there’s no room for complacency. It’s now up to Monica and Marcus to decide which five chefs have done enough to progress and who will hang up their MasterChef apron and leave the competition.
The battle to become MasterChef: The Professionals champion is well and truly under way. Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
Christina is rudely awakened to present this episode from Taunton in Somerset, where a huge antiques centre beckons for two teams of shoppers. In red are friends Aimi and Neil, and in blue are siblings Joe and Bella. With expert Ben Cooper by their side, the reds wonder whether they can cut a deal with an old knife box, while the blues and Danny Sebastian ponder over a wooden propeller – but aerospace engineer Joe doesn’t think it’ll fly at auction.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn is Sara from Crewe, with a remarkable relic of both sporting triumph and personal memory – her father Ronnie Cope’s 1958 FA Cup final shirt, when he played for Manchester United as one of the famed Busby Babes. Just months after the tragic Munich air disaster, Ronnie and his teammates defied the odds to reach Wembley. But the vivid red shirt was later left in a garage, used for painting and faded by sunlight. Textile conservator Rebecca Bissonnet faces the challenge of bringing the shirt back to the deep Manchester United red, while honouring its unique history.
Next, Judy and her daughter Laura bring in a small Bible with enormous meaning. It once belonged to Judy’s grandmother Florence, who was imprisoned with her children in the Lunghua Civilian Assembly Centre in Shanghai during the Second World War. When Florence fell ill, the three children – including Judy’s mother Mildred – were left to fend for themselves, and this fragile book was a source of comfort during years of hardship. Bookbinder Chris Shaw works delicately to preserve its battered pages and weathered covers, creating a fitting tribute to Florence and her descendants.
From Southampton, Munwar Hussain arrives with a beautiful but damaged Punjabi hookah once belonging to his grandfather Ghulam Farida, a farmer in Pakistan who lived to the age of 107. Munwar was very close to his grandfather and remembers this ornate smoking device as his constant companion. Silversmith Brenton West must repair its intricate metalwork and missing parts, while preserving the traces of Ghulam’s own repairs – the personal signature of a man who meant the world to his grandson.
Finally, brother and sister David and Lee from Huddersfield present an extraordinary automaton: a miniature watchmaker at work in his shop. Once the pride of their father’s clock repair business in Bradford, it sat in the window for decades, delighting customers and children alike. Now long silent, it is entrusted to the all-round talents of organ restorer David Burville to restore its complex mechanism and delicate movements and return this cherished figure to life.

From mighty, windswept cliffs to lush, sub-tropical gardens, the islands off the west coast of Ireland are extraordinary in their diversity. On the Aran Islands, Ardal learns from a practising monk of their ancient Christian heritage while, all around, a remarkable range of flora blooms, encouraged by traditional farming methods.
Continuing south, Ardal visits the abandoned Great Blasket Island, former home to Irish author Peig Sayers, now home to a thriving seal colony and two young caretakers. programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc:
Every chef dreams of a Michelin star. Episode two of Rise of the Rockstar Chef follows the hunt for that recognition, and for the leap that separates the great from the legendary. Moving from one star to two is hard, but the hardest jump of all is from two to three.
Marco Pierre White made that leap, becoming the first British chef to win three Michelin stars, and the youngest ever to do so. The episode explores what the pursuit demanded and what it cost. Marco reflects on the price of perfection. and how success also brings a rupture. Gordon Ramsay, who learned his craft under Marco, leaves to build his own name, and both men look back on the emotion of that parting. When menus from Aubergine begin appearing on Marco's desk, the friendship is over.
Gordon recounts the story of the stealing of the restaurant’s reservation book, the crown jewels of any restaurant, revealing just how bitter the split became. Marcus Wareing, Gordon's first employee, recalls the early days of Gordon's kitchen and the fierce ambition driving it.
As the 90s unfold, Heston Blumenthal’s drive, creativity and uncompromising pursuit of excellence transforms modern British cuisine. Heston cooks in a completely different way, and his food blows minds. It is pure theatre, with equipment unlike anything seen in a normal kitchen. Dishes such as the triple-cooked chip, taking two years to perfect, went on to change not just food but kitchens in restaurants and at home. With the opening of The Fat Duck, his home is on the line, and the need for success is huge.
Meanwhile, the empires expand. Marco and Gordon take over the kitchens of some of London's top hotels, and their restaurants become the places to be. Marco’s restaurant Titanic draws the Spice Girls, Oasis, footballers and the tabloids, with as many as 4,000 guests passing through in a single night - a 90s Studio 54. Contributors describe the energy of those years, and the revolutionary push for creativity in ways never seen before. When Heston is crowned the number one chef in the world, he voices the immensity of the pressure, his inferiority complex and the highs and lows of extreme success. Presenter - Ellie Taylor Executive Producer - Rhe-an Archibald Series Editor - Richard Berkshire Series Producer - Ross Proudfoot.

programme.title: BBC Children in Need
programme.sub-title: Sian Eleri’s BBC Children in Need Road Trip ║ 2026
programme.desc:
Radio 1 presenter Sian Eleri takes on an almighty challenge when BBC Children in Need’s Pudsey Bear sends her on a Wales-wide road trip. Her mission is to find six Children in Need-funded projects across Wales that support the development and well-being of young people. But Pudsey doesn’t make it easy. Each step of the way, she must solve one of Pudsey’s riddles before she can proceed to her next destination. The bear has also roped in BBC 1’s Morning Live presenter Gethin Jones and Radio 2’s early breakfast show host Owain Wyn Evans to bamboozle Sian on her journey.
The first project is at Tal Y Sarn farm on Anglesey, where BBC Children in Need-funded gymnastics sessions helped 18-year-old Abby overcome anxiety and an eating disorder. Next, Sian visits Theatr Clwyd in Mold. There, she meets Eleanor, who has global developmental delay and autism. Sian hears how the Theatr’s Fuse sessions give Eleanor an important creative outlet and safe space to make friends and build her confidence.
Sian’s third project is ASD Rainbows in Mountain Ash in the Cynon Valley. Here, BBC Children in Need funding pays for staffing for an after-school club which supports neurodivergent children like seven-year-old Olly. And in Cardiff Bay, Sian learns how a grant to the project Silkfutures, to support rap music sessions, has helped develop many young people’s self-confidence and given them the space to express themselves freely.
Next is Talking Hands, a charity in Swansea that teaches British Sign Language and supports deaf youngsters in Wales like eight-year-old Tom. Sian’s final project is Surfability. Based at Caswell Bay beach on the Gower peninsula, it helps children with additional needs and their siblings go surfing together. Here, the Radio 1 presenter has the chance to meet twin brothers Jakey and Ethan and see how Jakey, who has Down’s syndrome and is non-verbal, takes to the surfboard like a duck to water.
Along the way, Sian’s resilience is tested when she takes up pottery, mountain biking, surfing and open-air swimming before being reunited with Pudsey, who surprises her with an end-of-road trip wrap party.

Final day highlights as the DP World Tour season reaches its climax. The winner of the Race to Dubai is crowned, with Northern Ireland’s Rory McIlroy having won the last four editions. McIlroy has won seven Race to Dubai titles, putting him one behind Colin Montgomerie’s all-time record.
Spain’s Engenio Chacarra has enjoyed an incredible breakout season, and the USA’s Patrick Reed is firmly in the mix with two wins to his name. Open champion Ryan Fox and PGA champion Aaron Rai also tee it up on the Earth Course at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai.
The top ten DP World Tour members not already exempt will earn a PGA Tour card for the 2027 season. Presenter - Sarah Mulkerrins Editor - Jamie Gavin.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc:
Eva takes a boat trip down the Seine with chef Eric Ripert and writer Lindsey Tramuta. Together, they explore the story of French gastronomy through a seven-course fine dining meal.
At the heart of this delicious story is one man – Auguste Escoffier. He dominated every aspect of gastronomy, inventing and improving hundreds of classic dishes, bringing order to chaos in the kitchen with his military-style brigade and revolutionising front of house. Escoffier put French haute cuisine on the global map.

programme.sub-title: River Tees, County Durham - Trout ║ S9E4/6
programme.desc:
Bob and Paul are in County Durham, fishing the River Tees for a rare species of wild brown trout.
They navigate the area through the lens of a six-year-old Bob as he takes Paul on a trip along the landscapes of his youth. Bob lost his dad when he was very young, but some of the memories he holds dear to him are of the fishing trips they used to go on.
Later, Bob invites their old friend Reece Shearsmith to dinner, who has some particularly spooky local tales to tell them about the River Tees. programme.title: Rewarding
programme.desc:
Another beautiful morning at Beacon Fold, Mid Ulster’s premier private domiciliary care facility. A worn-out Francis shows colleagues Fidelma and Cyril the video of Clive, their last team lead, having a nervous breakdown and quitting mid-shift. Francis begs them to help the new team lead last the day. And of course, give client Cal a good birthday and survive the latest inspection from social worker Nicola.
New team lead Sinead arrives, prepped and ready for the first day of the job she’s spent three years studying social care for. Sadly, Beacon Fold is a little more run-down than the pictures on the brochure. Sinead meets her new team – hard-edged Fidelma and pathological small-talker Cyril – and tries to give them a motivational pep talk, but they’ve seen enough new hires crash and burn on their first day to know not to pay any attention.
As for the clients: Martina hasn’t left her room in days and has declared a hunger strike after seeing photos of her ex getting engaged. Joe’s acting out after a visit from his alcoholic mum, and it’s Cal’s birthday, which is always one wrong move away from disaster.
As Francis gives Sinead the grand tour of the facility, she realises it’s a long way from the glossy brochure. Meanwhile, social worker Nicola has news for Sinead when she drops in for a surprise inspection and tells her that Beacon Fold is going into special measures. Six months to turn it around, or the staff lose their jobs and the clients lose their care. Sinead, always a fan of a challenge, says she can do it in three months, an offer that Nicola happily accepts. And if Sinead doesn’t want her colleagues to quit right now, she recommends keeping the imminent closure a secret. programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc:
Relive some of the biggest hits of 1996 with these Top of the Pops classic performances. Summer hits were aplenty with Peter Andre, Gina G and Los Del Rio all bringing sunshine to Elstree. Hooks in hip-hop proved dominant with Dr Dre, Blackstreet, Mark Morrison, Toni Braxton and the Fugees all scoring huge hits. Britpop was still booming, with Oasis continuing to dominate singles sales with Sleeper hot on their heels. Global dance classics were born courtesy of Faithless and Robert Miles, and add into the mix the awesome arrival of Spice Girls, plus many more, and it’s not a year to miss.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.sub-title: Fire and Floods: Our Extreme Weather
programme.desc:
Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain.
The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, looks at whether enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate, and asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change? programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s quarter-final time again as the standout chefs from this week’s heats come together for another battle in the kitchen. The stakes are higher, the challenges more demanding, and the judges’ expectations are greater than ever.
First up is the invention test, where the chefs must make a surprise ingredient the star of the show. This time, it’s saffron, one of the world’s most-prized spices, renowned for its distinctive aroma, delicate floral notes and rich golden hue. But its extraordinary character comes with a challenge. Too little and its subtle flavour can disappear, but too much or poorly handled and it can overwhelm a dish with bitterness. The chefs must find the perfect balance, using their creativity and instinct to showcase saffron at its best. With just 70 minutes to cook and serve, can they transform this precious ingredient into something truly exceptional?
Next, the chefs face one of their toughest tests yet, cooking a two-course menu for three of the country’s leading food writers and critics, Leyla Kazim, Xanthe Clay and David Ellis. These seasoned critics know what separates a competent chef from a potential star, and this is a chance for the competitors to demonstrate the depth of their talent, with dishes that combine outstanding flavour, technical skill and individuality.
Taking the critics’ feedback into account, Marcus and Monica must now decide who has done enough to secure a place in knockout week. With the competition entering its most demanding phase, only the chefs who consistently deliver at the highest level will remain in the race for the coveted crown. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
International Men’s Day was established in 1999 to highlight positive male role models and raise awareness of men’s health and wellbeing. Ahead of this year’s event, Sean Fletcher is in Leeds exploring what it means to be a man in modern society, and how faith, friendship and a sense of purpose can help men thrive in mind, body and spirit.
He meets rugby league legend Jamie Jones-Buchanan, now CEO of Leeds Rhinos, where he made 421 appearances, as well as representing England and Great Britain. Jamie reflects on growing up without a father figure in one of the UK’s most deprived areas, and how rugby and his Christian faith provided positive male role models, and a sense of belonging and purpose. He challenges stereotypes of the macho rugby player, and his passion for helping the next generation comes to life during a training session.
In the Welsh valleys, Pastor John Funnell reflects on the extraordinary number of young men joining his congregation. John left a highly paid career after becoming a Christian and moved to one of Europe’s most deprived communities. He explains how his church offers practical skills, mentoring, friendship and faith, helping men see that their past does not have to determine their future.
Back in Leeds, Sean meets Chris Sayburn, a minister and renowned worship leader who spent 12 years living with chronic pain following complications after spinal surgery. He tells Sean how exercise and faith have helped him rebuild his life and how a community of men became a lifeline.
With uplifting hymns and songs from around the UK.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The open ocean is the largest wilderness on earth. Covering more than half of the planet's surface, it appears at first glance to be an endless blue desert. Yet hidden here are some of the most extraordinary animals.
We uncover the surprising strategies, epic journeys and remarkable resilience that allows life to thrive here. From wandering predators and drifting castaways to giant whales and tiny turtle hatchlings, it is a world where life survives against the odds.
The journey begins far beyond the sight of land, where California sea lions travel miles into the Pacific in search of seasonal, rich fishing grounds. Here, they join one of the open ocean's great feeding spectacles as black skipjack tuna, mahi-mahi and seabirds converge on vast schools of fish in a dramatic battle for a meal.
Some animals aren’t just visitors here; they spend their entire lives in this immense expanse. Rough-toothed dolphins have roamed the oceans since before woolly mammoths walked the earth, and yet we know very little about them. To help find food, they use sophisticated teamwork and ingenious hunting techniques that have rarely been witnessed.
Although the open ocean seems like a featureless expanse, it is shaped by powerful currents that flow across the globe like invisible rivers. These currents transport animals, nutrients and entire ecosystems across immense distances. For ocean drifters such as Smith's swimming crabs, the currents are both a lifeline and a gamble, carrying them through a world where danger can appear without warning.
Currents also drive one of the largest floating ecosystems on the planet. Today, the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt stretches over 5,000 miles across the ocean. But changing conditions are sweeping unprecedented amounts of this seaweed onto coastlines throughout the Caribbean. On the beaches of Mexico, turtle hatchlings emerging from their nests face a daunting new obstacle as mountains of sargassum block their path to the sea. Their struggle reveals how changes in the open ocean can have profound consequences far beyond the horizon.
In the Pacific, we follow one of nature's greatest aerial pirates, a frigatebird mother raising her chick alone.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here.
Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey - black-necked swans.
Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace - a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves.
As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable - they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before.
As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.sub-title: Fire and Floods: Our Extreme Weather
programme.desc:
Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain.
The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, looks at whether enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate, and asks, as the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies, or do they remain committed to tackling climate change? programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s quarter-final time again as the standout chefs from this week’s heats come together for another battle in the kitchen. The stakes are higher, the challenges more demanding, and the judges’ expectations are greater than ever.
First up is the invention test, where the chefs must make a surprise ingredient the star of the show. This time, it’s saffron, one of the world’s most-prized spices, renowned for its distinctive aroma, delicate floral notes and rich golden hue. But its extraordinary character comes with a challenge. Too little and its subtle flavour can disappear, but too much or poorly handled and it can overwhelm a dish with bitterness. The chefs must find the perfect balance, using their creativity and instinct to showcase saffron at its best. With just 70 minutes to cook and serve, can they transform this precious ingredient into something truly exceptional?
Next, the chefs face one of their toughest tests yet, cooking a two-course menu for three of the country’s leading food writers and critics, Leyla Kazim, Xanthe Clay and David Ellis. These seasoned critics know what separates a competent chef from a potential star, and this is a chance for the competitors to demonstrate the depth of their talent, with dishes that combine outstanding flavour, technical skill and individuality.
Taking the critics’ feedback into account, Marcus and Monica must now decide who has done enough to secure a place in knockout week. With the competition entering its most demanding phase, only the chefs who consistently deliver at the highest level will remain in the race for the coveted crown. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
International Men’s Day was established in 1999 to highlight positive male role models and raise awareness of men’s health and wellbeing. Ahead of this year’s event, Sean Fletcher is in Leeds exploring what it means to be a man in modern society, and how faith, friendship and a sense of purpose can help men thrive in mind, body and spirit.
He meets rugby league legend Jamie Jones-Buchanan, now CEO of Leeds Rhinos, where he made 421 appearances, as well as representing England and Great Britain. Jamie reflects on growing up without a father figure in one of the UK’s most deprived areas, and how rugby and his Christian faith provided positive male role models, and a sense of belonging and purpose. He challenges stereotypes of the macho rugby player, and his passion for helping the next generation comes to life during a training session.
In the Welsh valleys, Pastor John Funnell reflects on the extraordinary number of young men joining his congregation. John left a highly paid career after becoming a Christian and moved to one of Europe’s most deprived communities. He explains how his church offers practical skills, mentoring, friendship and faith, helping men see that their past does not have to determine their future.
Back in Leeds, Sean meets Chris Sayburn, a minister and renowned worship leader who spent 12 years living with chronic pain following complications after spinal surgery. He tells Sean how exercise and faith have helped him rebuild his life and how a community of men became a lifeline.
With uplifting hymns and songs from around the UK.
1. Sweet Heart of Jesus - Leeds Cathedral 2. Amazing Grace - The Kingdom Choir 3. Facing a Task Unfinished - Lisburn Cathedral 4. Lord of All Hopefulness - Chris Sayburn and Friends 5. programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The open ocean is the largest wilderness on earth. Covering more than half of the planet's surface, it appears at first glance to be an endless blue desert. Yet hidden here are some of the most extraordinary animals.
We uncover the surprising strategies, epic journeys and remarkable resilience that allows life to thrive here. From wandering predators and drifting castaways to giant whales and tiny turtle hatchlings, it is a world where life survives against the odds.
The journey begins far beyond the sight of land, where California sea lions travel miles into the Pacific in search of seasonal, rich fishing grounds. Here, they join one of the open ocean's great feeding spectacles as black skipjack tuna, mahi-mahi and seabirds converge on vast schools of fish in a dramatic battle for a meal.
Some animals aren’t just visitors here; they spend their entire lives in this immense expanse. Rough-toothed dolphins have roamed the oceans since before woolly mammoths walked the earth, and yet we know very little about them. To help find food, they use sophisticated teamwork and ingenious hunting techniques that have rarely been witnessed.
Although the open ocean seems like a featureless expanse, it is shaped by powerful currents that flow across the globe like invisible rivers. These currents transport animals, nutrients and entire ecosystems across immense distances. For ocean drifters such as Smith's swimming crabs, the currents are both a lifeline and a gamble, carrying them through a world where danger can appear without warning.
Currents also drive one of the largest floating ecosystems on the planet. Today, the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt stretches over 5,000 miles across the ocean. But changing conditions are sweeping unprecedented amounts of this seaweed onto coastlines throughout the Caribbean. On the beaches of Mexico, turtle hatchlings emerging from their nests face a daunting new obstacle as mountains of sargassum block their path to the sea. Their struggle reveals how changes in the open ocean can have profound consequences far beyond the horizon.
In the Pacific, we follow one of nature's greatest aerial pirates, a frigatebird mother raising her chick alone.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here.
Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey - black-necked swans.
Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace - a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves.
As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable - they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before.
As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres.

He is put to work behind the scenes at Glasgow's circular subway, explores the future of shipbuilding on the Clyde. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo falls into line with the University of Glasgow's Officer Training Corps. Founded in the early 20th century, the Corps flourishes today and Michael joins students for drill. From Glasgow, Michael heads west along the Firth of Clyde to Helensburgh, where he discovers a pioneering group of artists known as the Glasgow Boys. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E11 ║ Warwick to Radley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: n Warwick's medieval castle he uncovers the scene of an extravagant and scandalous ball, which changed the life of its hostess, Daisy Greville, Countess of Warwick.At Cowley, Michael marvels at a spectacularly automated state-of-the-art production line producing 1,000 Minis a day and probes the pre-First World War origins of the Morris Oxford. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E12 ║ Reading to Taplow ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo picks up his rail journey from Warwick to Rye along the River Thames. In Reading, he traces the origins of education for workers. Messing about in boats is the name of the game in Henley on Thames, where Michael slips into a launch to hear about the world-famous regatta. Afternoon tea on the bank offers a chance to hear about four heroes of early 20th-century literary classic `The Wind in the Willows'. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Teleshopping
programme.desc: Shopping from home.

programme.title: Africa from Above
programme.desc: An aerial adventure through the landlocked country of Zambia that takes in sights including the largest migration of mammals on Earth, the huge Victoria Falls, and the meandering Zambezi River.

programme.title: Africa from Above
programme.desc: Explores the great diversity in natural landscapes and life in the country of Mozambique through visits to the country's Indian Ocean coastline, mountain rainforests, and Zembezi River delta.

programme.title: Africa from Above
programme.desc: Journeys through the diverse landscapes, rich cultures and linguistic customs, and remarkable flora and fauna of Cameroon, a country that sits at the crossroads of West and Central Africa. Tom Vogt.

programme.title: Africa from Above
programme.desc: Explores the great variation in the landscapes of Botswana. Includes visits to the salt pans of the Makgadikgadi, the maze of marshlands and floodplains within the Okavango Delta, and the Kalahari Desert. Tom Vogt.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Reno to Napa Valley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Beginning in the Silver State of Nevada, Michael takes to the skies over the dramatic Sierra Nevada mountain range. At Lake Tahoe, he hears of the first European explorer, known as `The Pathfinder', whose discovery opened up the west for settlement. Travelling on the historic Virginia and Truckee heritage line, Michael investigates the vast deposits of silver and gold ore on which Virginia City was built. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.desc: Armed with his trusty Appleton's Guide, Michael Portillo reaches San Francisco, where he boards one of the city's iconic cable cars. Behind the scenes in the engineering powerhouse, he uncovers the street cars' secret to scaling the city's famously steep hills. In the Presidio neighbourhood, a leading publisher introduces Michael to San Francisco's long tradition of fine printing and book-making. Michael takes the opportunity to have his own treasured book appraised. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Berkeley to Santa Cruz ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Following his Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo makes a trip to the jewel in the crown of America's National Parks, Yosemite, to behold its towering granite cliffs, its giant sequoia trees and cascading waterfalls. He discovers how early conservationists fought to protect it in law and encounters a `buffalo soldier' in the heart of the forest. In Berkeley, Michael uncovers a catastrophic event, which hit the city of San Francisco hard in 1906. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Monterey to Los Angeles ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Steered by his late 19th-century Appleton's guidebook, Michael Portillo continues through southern California aboard the Coast Starlight rail service. In the historic port of Monterey, Michael raises the Bear Flag of the one-time Republic of California and above it, the Stars and Stripes. He discovers the city's Spanish and Mexican heritage and traces how the former fishing port described as `stinking and decrepit' in John Steinbeck's novel, `Cannery Row', has become a beacon for tourists. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Los Angeles to San Diego ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Michael Portillo strikes oil in the suburbs of Los Angeles, contemplates his navel in the orange groves of Riverside, makes a California roll and paints a pretty picture in Laguna Beach. It is Mexican Independence Day and the locals are celebrating the country's hard-won independence from Spain in the early 19th century. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: S3E2 ║ Boston to Concord ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's nineteenth-century Appleton's guidebook leads him to the Parker House Hotel, where in his best pinny, he whisks up a Boston cream pie. In the fine dome atop Massachusetts General Hospital, where no-one could hear the screaming, Michael discovers the scene of grisly surgery, first made bearable, in 1846, by a miraculous new substance. North of Boston, in Salem, Michael is caught up in a witch hunt. Chris Bairstow - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Plymouth to New London ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Guided by his Appleton's and tracing the footsteps of the Pilgrim Fathers, Michael Portillo heads for Plymouth, the `home town' of America. He learns how indigenous tribes of Wamponoag people taught newly arrived settlers to live off the land, inspiring one of the biggest holidays in today's American calendar. Chris Bairstow - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: New Haven to Plattsburgh: Reversion ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Armed with his Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo continues his rail journey through Connecticut and New England. He takes a crash course in rowing in New Haven, where college teams from Yale and Harvard have battled for victory on the water since 1852. In Vermont, Michael visits a 19th-century farm, where the rich milk from prized Jersey cows imported from the British Isles supplied a thriving butter industry. Chris Bairstow - Director Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Frozen Planet
programme.desc: It is high summer in the polar regions, and the sun never sets. Vast hordes of summer visitors cram a lifetime of drama into one long, magical day; they must feed, fight and rear their young in this brief window of plenty. Summer is a tough time for the polar bear family, as their ice world melts away and the cubs take their first swimming lesson. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Frozen Planet
programme.desc: Polar landscapes in autumn are transformed as the big freeze returns. Most animals leave on epic journeys, some now battle to breed, and for the hardy few it's a time of opportunity. In the Arctic, polar bears gather in large numbers on the coast to wait for the return of the ice. Tempers soon fray and violent contests break out. Off the coast 2,000 beluga whales head for a special estuary, a gigantic `whale spa'. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Frozen Planet
programme.desc: Winter is the greatest test for life in the polar regions, as temperatures plummet to 70 below and winds reach 200kph. Only a few remarkable survivors gamble on remaining in these extreme conditions. In the Arctic, a female polar bear treks into the mountains to give birth. Out on the frozen ocean, the entire population of the world's spectacled eider ducks braves the winter in a giant ice hole. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Frozen Planet
programme.sub-title: S1E6 ║ The Last Frontier ║ Documentary / Nature ║ 2011
programme.desc: Revealing the extraordinary riches and wonders of the polar regions that have kept people visiting them for thousands of years. Today, their survival relies on a combination of ancient wisdom and cutting-edge science. Most Arctic people live in Siberia, either in cities like Norilsk - the coldest city on earth - or out on the tundra, where tribes like the Dogan survive by herding reindeer. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: In Belfast's grand Edwardian City Hall, Michael investigates the scene of a watershed moment in Irish history and hears how thousands of Ulster Protestants were mobilised by train to sign a document pledging opposition to Home Rule for Ireland. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving from the seaport of Larne Michael reaches Stranraerand the Mull of Galloway, where in a lighthouse built by railway engineer, Robert Stevenson, he discovers a magnificent machine, installed at the turn of the 20th century. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his journey through western Scotland by exploring the industrial heartland of Glasgow and its mighty River Clyde before taking the ferry to the island of Cumbrae. He is put to work behind the scenes at Glasgow's circular subway, explores the future of shipbuilding on the Clyde. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo falls into line with the University of Glasgow's Officer Training Corps. Founded in the early 20th century, the Corps flourishes today and Michael joins students for drill. From Glasgow, Michael heads west along the Firth of Clyde to Helensburgh, where he discovers a pioneering group of artists known as the Glasgow Boys. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E11 ║ Warwick to Radley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: n Warwick's medieval castle he uncovers the scene of an extravagant and scandalous ball, which changed the life of its hostess, Daisy Greville, Countess of Warwick.At Cowley, Michael marvels at a spectacularly automated state-of-the-art production line producing 1,000 Minis a day and probes the pre-First World War origins of the Morris Oxford. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E12 ║ Reading to Taplow ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo picks up his rail journey from Warwick to Rye along the River Thames. In Reading, he traces the origins of education for workers. Messing about in boats is the name of the game in Henley on Thames, where Michael slips into a launch to hear about the world-famous regatta. Afternoon tea on the bank offers a chance to hear about four heroes of early 20th-century literary classic `The Wind in the Willows'. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.desc: Shopping from home.

programme.title: Africa from Above
programme.desc: An aerial adventure through the landlocked country of Zambia that takes in sights including the largest migration of mammals on Earth, the huge Victoria Falls, and the meandering Zambezi River.

programme.title: Africa from Above
programme.desc: Explores the great diversity in natural landscapes and life in the country of Mozambique through visits to the country's Indian Ocean coastline, mountain rainforests, and Zembezi River delta.

programme.title: Africa from Above
programme.desc: Journeys through the diverse landscapes, rich cultures and linguistic customs, and remarkable flora and fauna of Cameroon, a country that sits at the crossroads of West and Central Africa. Tom Vogt.

programme.title: Africa from Above
programme.desc: Explores the great variation in the landscapes of Botswana. Includes visits to the salt pans of the Makgadikgadi, the maze of marshlands and floodplains within the Okavango Delta, and the Kalahari Desert. Tom Vogt.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Reno to Napa Valley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Beginning in the Silver State of Nevada, Michael takes to the skies over the dramatic Sierra Nevada mountain range. At Lake Tahoe, he hears of the first European explorer, known as `The Pathfinder', whose discovery opened up the west for settlement. Travelling on the historic Virginia and Truckee heritage line, Michael investigates the vast deposits of silver and gold ore on which Virginia City was built. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.desc: Armed with his trusty Appleton's Guide, Michael Portillo reaches San Francisco, where he boards one of the city's iconic cable cars. Behind the scenes in the engineering powerhouse, he uncovers the street cars' secret to scaling the city's famously steep hills. In the Presidio neighbourhood, a leading publisher introduces Michael to San Francisco's long tradition of fine printing and book-making. Michael takes the opportunity to have his own treasured book appraised. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Berkeley to Santa Cruz ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Following his Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo makes a trip to the jewel in the crown of America's National Parks, Yosemite, to behold its towering granite cliffs, its giant sequoia trees and cascading waterfalls. He discovers how early conservationists fought to protect it in law and encounters a `buffalo soldier' in the heart of the forest. In Berkeley, Michael uncovers a catastrophic event, which hit the city of San Francisco hard in 1906. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Monterey to Los Angeles ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Steered by his late 19th-century Appleton's guidebook, Michael Portillo continues through southern California aboard the Coast Starlight rail service. In the historic port of Monterey, Michael raises the Bear Flag of the one-time Republic of California and above it, the Stars and Stripes. He discovers the city's Spanish and Mexican heritage and traces how the former fishing port described as `stinking and decrepit' in John Steinbeck's novel, `Cannery Row', has become a beacon for tourists. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Los Angeles to San Diego ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Michael Portillo strikes oil in the suburbs of Los Angeles, contemplates his navel in the orange groves of Riverside, makes a California roll and paints a pretty picture in Laguna Beach. It is Mexican Independence Day and the locals are celebrating the country's hard-won independence from Spain in the early 19th century. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: S3E2 ║ Boston to Concord ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's nineteenth-century Appleton's guidebook leads him to the Parker House Hotel, where in his best pinny, he whisks up a Boston cream pie. In the fine dome atop Massachusetts General Hospital, where no-one could hear the screaming, Michael discovers the scene of grisly surgery, first made bearable, in 1846, by a miraculous new substance. North of Boston, in Salem, Michael is caught up in a witch hunt. Chris Bairstow - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Plymouth to New London ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Guided by his Appleton's and tracing the footsteps of the Pilgrim Fathers, Michael Portillo heads for Plymouth, the `home town' of America. He learns how indigenous tribes of Wamponoag people taught newly arrived settlers to live off the land, inspiring one of the biggest holidays in today's American calendar. Chris Bairstow - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: New Haven to Plattsburgh: Reversion ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Armed with his Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo continues his rail journey through Connecticut and New England. He takes a crash course in rowing in New Haven, where college teams from Yale and Harvard have battled for victory on the water since 1852. In Vermont, Michael visits a 19th-century farm, where the rich milk from prized Jersey cows imported from the British Isles supplied a thriving butter industry. Chris Bairstow - Director Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Inside Bentley: A Great British Motor Car
programme.desc: Bentley Motors have been building bespoke cars for the rich and famous for almost a century, and for the first time in their long history, the doors of its historic home in northwest England have been opened to the cameras. Joe Lister - Director John Thomson - Narrator.

programme.title: Frozen Planet
programme.desc: It is high summer in the polar regions, and the sun never sets. Vast hordes of summer visitors cram a lifetime of drama into one long, magical day; they must feed, fight and rear their young in this brief window of plenty. Summer is a tough time for the polar bear family, as their ice world melts away and the cubs take their first swimming lesson. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Frozen Planet
programme.desc: Polar landscapes in autumn are transformed as the big freeze returns. Most animals leave on epic journeys, some now battle to breed, and for the hardy few it's a time of opportunity. In the Arctic, polar bears gather in large numbers on the coast to wait for the return of the ice. Tempers soon fray and violent contests break out. Off the coast 2,000 beluga whales head for a special estuary, a gigantic `whale spa'. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Frozen Planet
programme.desc: Winter is the greatest test for life in the polar regions, as temperatures plummet to 70 below and winds reach 200kph. Only a few remarkable survivors gamble on remaining in these extreme conditions. In the Arctic, a female polar bear treks into the mountains to give birth. Out on the frozen ocean, the entire population of the world's spectacled eider ducks braves the winter in a giant ice hole. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Frozen Planet
programme.sub-title: S1E6 ║ The Last Frontier ║ Documentary / Nature ║ 2011
programme.desc: Revealing the extraordinary riches and wonders of the polar regions that have kept people visiting them for thousands of years. Today, their survival relies on a combination of ancient wisdom and cutting-edge science. Most Arctic people live in Siberia, either in cities like Norilsk - the coldest city on earth - or out on the tundra, where tribes like the Dogan survive by herding reindeer. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.desc: Michael begins his American adventure on Manhattan Island. Starting at New York's Grand Central Terminal, he boards the Manhattan subway system, the busiest rail transit system in the US. Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.desc: Beginning in Brooklyn, Michael hears the moving story behind the construction of the world's first steel suspension bridge high above the East River. Below ground, he investigates the arrival of New York City's first subway and the dangers faced by the men who built it: the `sandhogs'. Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: New York City to Albany ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2016
programme.desc: Michael follows America's iconic River Hudson north through New York State. Beginning at New York City's Penn Station, Michael rides the national rail carrier service, Amtrak. He hears from Amtrak's police chief how railroad policing began to tackle the nation's most notorious train robbers, among them Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid. Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Schenectady to Niagara Falls ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2016
programme.desc: Michael Portillo braves the awesome power and drenching spray of Niagara Falls in the `Maid of the Mist' to share what artists, daredevils and millions of tourists have billed as one of the most spectacular experiences on the planet. Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Abandoned Engineering

programme.title: Don't Tell the Bride
programme.desc: Groom Ian uses the £12,000 budget to fly him and his two best men out to Thailand to buy cut-price suits and a bargain wedding dress - and have an exotic stag do too. However, his trip may not pay off in the long run for his down-to-earth bride Jay.

programme.title: Don't Tell the Bride
programme.desc: Rock star-turned-zookeeper Scott plans a jungle-themed wedding for his bride-to-be Verity - and spends only £100 on a wedding dress for her, and £1,800 on life-size plastic animals to decorate their reception.

Recently, it enjoyed its busiest summer, scooping 146 billion dots and making an annual revenue of $300million. But, before that, in 2012, the company was on the brink of bankruptcy, until owner and CEO Scott Fischer turned its fortunes around. Here, he infiltrates his workforce to find out if his expanding empire has the manpower to cope. Their success meant they could afford to purchase the location next door in the 1990s, naming it Mama Maria after John's mother, who died in 2002. But when he lost his father as well, John became overwhelmed by the responsibility of running both establishments and his livelihood is at risk.

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares USA
programme.sub-title: S6E5 ║ Barefoot Bob's ║ Cooking, Leisure Hobbies

With the restaurant and marriage on the line, Gordon tries to help turn things around before it's too late.

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares USA

programme.desc: Gordon Ramsay revisits three of the most difficult cases he has taken on since the series began. When he first visited owners Tommy and Dina DeFino, the business was struggling so badly that Tommy had completely lost his confidence and wife Dina had lost her patience. On his final stop, Gordon travels to Leone's in Montclair, New Jersey, where Rose Leone was depending on her lazy son Michael to run the restaurant.

programme.title: Kahin Pyar Na Ho Jaye
programme.desc: Prem is supposed to marry Nisha but she gets married to a rich NRI. He is devastated and takes to drinking. Later, he meets Priya and falls in love with her.

programme.title: Bunty Aur Babli
programme.desc: A small-town couple turns to con artistry to escape mediocrity, creating hilarious and daring scams. Their adventures make them legends until love, fame, and morality catch up with them.

programme.title: Bala
programme.desc: A young man battling premature balding faces ridicule and insecurity. Through humor and self-realization, he learns that confidence and self-acceptance define beauty beyond physical appearance.

programme.title: Golmaal 3
programme.desc: Cupid strikes when a single father meets college sweetheart Geeta in Goa. Their children go at war with each other, they find it hard to reunite.

programme.title: Luka Chupi
programme.desc: Guddu, a reporter in a local news channel, falls in love with Rashmi and asks her to marry him. However, things turn chaotic when they begin a live-in relationship and their family knows about it.

programme.title: Chhaava
programme.desc: After his father's death, warrior-king Sambhaji Maharaj fights Mughal forces under Aurangzeb to defend and preserve the Maratha Empire.

programme.title: Chandni Chowk To China
programme.desc: A humble cook from Delhi believes he's the reincarnation of a Chinese warrior. Thrust into an epic adventure, he discovers courage, identity, and humor in this martial arts comedy.

programme.title: Motichoor Chaknachoor
programme.desc: Anita dreams of marrying a foreign-settled man. She chooses Pushpinder, a Dubai-returned bachelor desperate for a bride, but their expectations clash in hilarious and heartfelt ways.

programme.title: Kaala Patthar
programme.desc: Vijay Singh is a disgraced former navy officer who is branded as a coward and forced to work at a coal mine out of guilt. However, he gets trapped with other miners after a flood hits them.

programme.title: Neal 'N' Nikki
programme.desc: Neal spends a month on vacation before getting married. He falls in love with Nikki. On his return, he finds that he is engaged to her cousin.

programme.title: Saathiya
programme.desc: Aditya and Suhani defy parental opposition to marry. Yet, their fairy-tale romance begins to crack under the strain of reality.

programme.title: Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani
programme.desc: A group of friends navigate love, dreams, and chaos. Their journey celebrates youth, friendship, and romance, creating memories that last forever.

programme.title: Gabbar Is Back
programme.desc: After being wronged by the city's corrupt administration, Aditya adopts the alias Gabbar and joins hands with honest officers to wage a fearless war against corruption and injustice.

programme.title: Ishaqzaade
programme.desc: Two lovers from rival political families defy hatred to be together. Their passionate romance turns tragic, revealing the destructive power of ego, violence, and forbidden love.

programme.title: Haathi Mere Saathi
programme.desc: A man and his elephants share a deep bond, but his love for animals strains his marriage. The touching story celebrates compassion, loyalty, and the harmony between humans and nature.

programme.title: The Big Bull
programme.desc: Hemant Shah, a man from a humble background, aspires to become rich. He soon devises a plan to exploit the loopholes in the banking system to fulfil his ambitions.

programme.title: Kabhi Kabhie
programme.desc: Amit and Pooja love each other but their parents are against their relationship. They decide to marry as per their parents' wishes. Things take a turn when they meet again after many years.

programme.title: The Great Indian Family
programme.desc: Ved Vyas Tripathi, aka Bhajan Kumar, is a devout Hindu man who faces an identity crisis and a personal dilemma when he discovers he is actually a Muslim by birth.

programme.title: Hadh Kar Di Aapne
programme.desc: Two travelers mistaken for a married couple fall in love amid chaos. Packed with situational humor and romance, it's a delightful comedy about destiny and unexpected connections.

programme.title: Sunny Sanskari Ki Tulsi Kumari
programme.desc: After their partners, Ananya and Vikram, heartlessly dump them to marry each other, Sunny and Tulsi form an unlikely alliance. Together, they plot to gatecrash their exes' big wedding.

programme.title: Blast Zone
programme.desc: A martial-arts-trained headmaster and his close family find their peaceful lives shattered when they unexpectedly tangle with a ruthless mercenary gang guarding a stash of stolen cash.

programme.title: Stree
programme.desc: A town is held in the grip of terror by tales of a mysterious woman who calls men by their name and then abducts them, leaving their clothes behind.

programme.title: Apradhi (1992)
programme.desc: A family is devastated after the sole bread-winner of the house is killed. When all hope seems to disappear, they are saved by a stranger who helps them in many ways. But he too has a secret.

programme.title: Namak Halaal
programme.desc: However, Arjun, a young hotel worker who serves Raja faithfully, learns of a plot to kill him and decides to save his boss at any cost.

programme.title: Veer-Zaara
programme.desc: The story of Squadron Leader Veer Pratap Singh and Zaara Haayat Khan, of Lahore, during conflict between India and Pakistan.

programme.title: Chhichhore
programme.desc: A tragic event reunites college friends as they reflect on friendship, success, and failure. Through humor and emotion, they learn that life's worth isn't defined by victory but by never giving up.

programme.title: Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani
programme.desc: Rocky and Rani face cultural clashes, traditions, and generational divides, proving that love thrives despite challenges and family conflicts.

programme.title: Garam Masala
programme.desc: Two flirty photographers juggle multiple girlfriends, leading to hilarious confusion. Witty dialogues and comic timing create a chaotic tale of deceit, friendship, and endless misunderstandings.

programme.title: Fighter
programme.desc: A team of brave Indian Air Force pilots unite to defend the nation from external threats. With spectacular aerial action, patriotism, and camaraderie, the film honors the spirit of warriors.

programme.title: Sailaab (1990)
programme.desc: Krishna, who suffers from memory loss, is under the care of Dr Sushma and soon, they fall in love and get married. However, things change when Krishna regains his memory and tries to kill Sushma.

programme.title: Chaloo Movie
programme.desc: The police raid a theatre where movie tickets are being sold in black.

programme.title: Nikaah
programme.desc: Afaque, who falls in love with Nilofar, is left heartbroken when she marries another man. Things take an unexpected turn when Nilofar gets divorced and Afaque offers her a job at his company.

programme.title: Hichki
programme.desc: A passionate teacher with Tourette syndrome turns her weakness into strength while inspiring underprivileged students. Her resilience and empathy redefine success and education.

programme.title: ABCD: Any Body Can Dance
programme.desc: Vishnu leads his dance team against powerful rivals, overcoming personal struggles, friendship conflicts and fierce competition to achieve national glory.

programme.title: Dangal
programme.desc: Former wrestler Mahavir Phogat trains his daughters to win a Commonwealth Games gold, defying societal norms to achieve his lifelong dream for India.
